messages:
alex: heads up — after a spot GPU node eviction in eu-west we started seeing intermittent name resolution failures for headless model services. traffic to the edge model pool dropped and some requests got 502/connection reset.

infra-bot: [alert] node/gpu-eu-spot-12 evicted (preempted) at 2039012330 — pods rescheduled to gpu-eu-standby-*.

maria: what exactly are the DNS errors? coredns logs? endpoint slices?

alex: quick paste of the coredns tail:```2026-03-18T10:05:12Z [INFO] plugin/loop: error on lookup "model-a.default.svc.cluster.local": SERVFAIL
2026-03-18T10:05:13Z [WARN] plugin/errors: 2 model-a.default.svc.cluster.local. A: no such host
```

alex: kubectl checks show endpoint objects exist but EndpointSlice for some services is empty on the new nodes:```$ kubectl get endpointslice -n default -o wide | grep model-a
model-a-xxxx  0  10s  0  0  <controller=discovery.k8s.io>
```

tim: hunch — kube-proxy on the nodes handling rescheduled pods might have stale iptables/ipvs rules referencing evicted node IPs. that can cause traffic to be SNATed incorrectly or dropped before coredns gets a working backend, which looks like DNS flapping from the app POV.

anya: can we check conntrack on the node that received traffic? run: `conntrack -L | grep <old-pod-ip>` and `sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep KUBE-SERVICES`

alex: ran conntrack and saw a bunch of ESTABLISHED entries still pointing at the old pod IPs. also noticed kube-proxy logs:```W03018 10:06:01.123 kube-proxy.go:123] failed to sync service default/model-a: could not find Endpoints for service model-a (cached)
```

maria: sounds like EndpointSlice controller didn't reconcile after node eviction. did the controller-manager OOM or get throttled? any spikes in control-plane CPU?

alex: control plane looked fine in metrics, but the edge cluster had high kube-apiserver latency for ~2m during the eviction. suspect race: pods rescheduled, endpoint objects created, but endpointslice controller missed updates and kube-proxy on some nodes didn't rebuild rules.

tim: quick mitigation: rotate kube-proxy on affected nodes (systemctl restart kube-proxy) and run `kubectl delete endpointslice <empty-slice>` so controller recreates them. also clear conntrack for stale pod IPs: `conntrack -D -d <old-pod-ip>` (careful).

sre-oncall: applying those now to eu-west nodes that have model traffic. doing conntrack prune first then kube-proxy restart on one node for canary.

maria: also add an automated check: after node eviction events, validate that EndpointSlices for headless services have >0 endpoints across new nodes within 30s, alert otherwise. this would catch controller hiccups early.

alex: confirmed — after conntrack prune + kube-proxy restart the model-a EndpointSlice repopulated and coredns SERVFAILs subsided. traffic back to normal. :tada:

anya: filing a follow-up issue: possible race between node eviction, endpointslice controller and kube-proxy rule reconciliation. propose a short runbook for oncall and add a post-eviction job to force endpointslice reconcilers if we see <threshold replicas.

maria: also note cost angle — spot evictions are fine but frequent evictions on edge pools increase churn and conntrack/iptables thrash. we should look at eviction rate per week and move noisy workloads to non-spot or reserved pools if >3 evictions/week.

alex: thanks all. I'll add the runbook steps + the alert to infra-monitoring and link the debug logs.

infra-bot: [note] runbook created: infra/runbooks/endpointslice-eviction-heuristics.md

maria: nice. please include the exact conntrack commands and safety warnings.

alex: will do, sharing the runbook PR shortly.
